answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token stake for a cooling-off period before it earns voting or task-allocation weight. A reputation delta then grows only through verified work and decays after failures, so minting many fresh accounts does not multiply influence. To capture the system, an attacker must buy and immobilize enough stake across identities, paying capital costs and risking slashing; a reef of cheap accounts alone gains little, while jade credentials remain costly to fake.
